name: Manuel John Johnson
summary: British positional astronomer and President of the Royal Astronomical Society known for tidal measurements at St. Helena.

name: Nevil Maskelyne
summary: Astronomer Royal who recorded tides at St. Helena in 1761 using a vertical staff method.

name: Charles Mason
summary: Associate of the Royal Society and assistant to Maskelyne during the 1761 St. Helena expedition.

name: Alexander Walker
summary: Governor of St. Helena who appointed Johnson to the observatory and supported tidal observations.

name: Fearon Fallows
summary: Director of the Cape Observatory who advised Johnson on tidal observations.

name: St. Helena
summary: Remote Atlantic island where Johnson conducted tidal and astronomical observations.

name: Jamestown
summary: Main settlement and landing place on St. Helena where tidal gauges were installed.

name: Cape of Good Hope
summary: Location of the observatory Johnson visited for advice in 1825–1826.

name: Royal Astronomical Society
summary: Learned society that awarded Johnson the Gold Medal and where he served as President.

name: Honourable East India Company
summary: Trading company that employed Johnson and funded the St. Helena Observatory.

name: St. Helena Observatory
summary: Astronomical facility on St. Helena founded by Walker and Johnson.

name: Royal Society of London
summary: Scientific academy that elected Johnson as a Fellow.

name: Johnson's tide gauge
summary: Unique instrument with sliding indices designed by Johnson to record tidal extrema.

name: Star catalogue (1835)
summary: Publication of stellar positions compiled by Johnson at St. Helena.
